solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bacchanalian Borgia's ticker-tape welcome

indicators.note: the phrase takes in and plays host to the run of letters, so welcome signals a word held within

explanation.surface: A Renaissance Borgia gets a parade with ticker-tape thrown from the windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcome' looks like part of the parade, but it is the signal: the letters run from the end of BORGIA'S into TICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchanalian revels, named for Bacchus, are wild drunken orgies, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Oscar finally adopts alias in Japanese city

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word adopts

parts.note: AKA, 'also known as', introduces an alias

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner takes a false name while staying in a Japanese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city on the island of Honshu, an example of a city in Japan.

clue.text: Travelling north in the shadow of Etna, villa-goers gad about

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
being in the shadow of the words means sitting within them, so the letters lie inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers in villas on the slopes of Etna wander about the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the shadow of' marks TNAVILLAG inside ETNA, VILLA-GOERS, and 'Travelling north' turns it round, as a down entry reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To gad about is to roam idly in search of fun, the same as the verb meaning to wander for pleasure.

clue.text: Medic in A&E beginning to need some cocaine in response to stress

indicators.note: in places the doctor inside the letters of the hospital department

parts.note: A&E is the British hospital accident and emergency department, written AE
a medic is a doctor, abbreviated DR

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of need

parts.note: a line is a measured dose of cocaine snorted by a user, so some cocaine is a line

explanation.surface: A doctor in the emergency room starts to need a hit of cocaine to cope with the pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is Britain's accident and emergency (ER) department. The second 'in' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal glands release this hormone as the body's fight-or-flight response to fear or strain.

clue.text: Grass and tree infested with insects

parts.note: the ti is a Pacific palm-like tree, a crossword regular
something mothy is full of moths, so infested with insects

explanation.surface: A lawn and a tree are both overrun with bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy is a meadow grass grown widely for hay, so it is an example of a grass.

clue.text: Bill's loving partner wearing fleeces and wraps

indicators.note: the fleeces are worn around the partner, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to fleece someone is to swindle them, so fleeces means cons
the phrase bill and coo pairs coo with bill as lovers' murmuring

explanation.surface: Someone's affectionate partner is dressed in fleeces and shawls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is the verb in 'bill and coo', to kiss and murmur like doves.
explanation.definitionFit: To cocoon something is to enclose it snugly, so as a verb it means wraps.

clue.text: Crusty tripe sandwiches lead to revulsion

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between two parts, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: tripe and guff both mean nonsense

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, here of revulsion

explanation.surface: A dish of tripe in bread is enough to turn the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' looks like food but means rubbish talk; 'sandwiches' carries the eating picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusty person is short-tempered and abrupt, the same manner as a gruff one.

clue.text: Pat left to enter British territory

indicators.note: to enter puts the abbreviation for left inside the territory

parts.note: Gib is the familiar short name for Gibraltar, a British overseas territory

explanation.surface: Someone called Pat leaves to go into a British overseas territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a person's name but is the adjective, as in a pat answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pat or slick answer comes too readily and sounds rehearsed, which is a facile reply.

clue.text: Duo spy Wendy shedding clothes to stand on head

indicators.note: taking the clothes off each word strips its outer letters, leaving the middle ones

explanation.surface: A spying pair and a woman called Wendy undress to do a headstand.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, so it ends up balanced on its top.

clue.text: Fire predecessor as things get worse?

definitions.text: Fire predecessor as things get worse?

parts.words: Fire predecessor as things get worse?
parts.note: the saying 'out of the ___ into the fire' describes going from bad to worse, so this item comes just before the fire

explanation.surface: What comes before the fire when matters deteriorate?
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names this kitchen utensil as the lesser hazard escaped before landing in the fire.

clue.text: More than competent Hedda blowing head off

indicators.note: Hedda Gabler shoots herself in Ibsen's play, and here she loses her first letter

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the title heroine of Ibsen's drama, so Hedda stands for her surname

explanation.surface: Ibsen's Hedda, who ends the play by shooting herself, is better than merely capable.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to Hedda Gabler's suicide by pistol at the end of Ibsen's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Abler is the comparative of able, which means competent, so it describes someone more capable.

clue.text: Can I rhyme "errant" and "plant"?

indicators.note: errant means straying from the proper course, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A poet wonders whether two awkward words can be made to rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a word to rhyme but means industrial equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant in the industrial sense is the heavy equipment of a factory, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Estrangement from state after a deception

indicators.note: after says the state comes behind the earlier pieces

parts.note: a lie is a deception
a nation is a state

explanation.surface: A country drifts away from another after being deceived.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is the state of being cut off or made hostile, the same as estrangement.

clue.text: Place of bliss, ecstasy and retreat

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A blissful spot combines rapture with a quiet hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden of Paradise is the archetypal place of perfect happiness.

clue.text: Getting jostled, but lads are coping with supporters

indicators.note: jostled letters are pushed about out of their order

explanation.surface: Boys in a crowd are being shoved but are managing to handle it alongside fellow fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coping' looks like 'managing' but is the capping on top of a wall; 'supporters' are not fans but balusters.
explanation.definitionFit: A balustrade is a rail or capping held up by a row of small pillars called balusters.

clue.text: Feel unwell on Friday, with extremes of torpidity and weakness

indicators.note: in an across entry, on means placed after

parts.note: to ail is to feel unwell

indicators.note: extremes are the first and last letters of torpidity

explanation.surface: Someone is sick at the end of the week, sluggish and feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Frailty is physical or moral feebleness, a synonym of weakness.

clue.text: Porky Pig limiting minutes working out

parts.note: porky means fat

indicators.note: limiting means bounding on both sides, so the pig encloses the minutes

parts.note: a hog is a pig
MIN is the abbreviation for minutes

explanation.surface: The cartoon Porky Pig cuts his time at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky Pig' reads as the cartoon character but splits into two pieces; 'working out' is not exercise but understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Fathoming a problem means getting to the bottom of it, i.e. understanding or solving it.

clue.text: Primate in frantic push to get fit

indicators.note: in places the primate inside the jumbled letters
frantic means wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A gorilla makes a desperate effort to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantic' sounds like the effort of the push, but it is the signal that the letters of push are scrambled around the primate.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape up is to improve one's condition, the phrasal verb used for getting into trim.

clue.text: French writer recollecting a 50 ounce English fruit

indicators.note: re-collecting means gathering together again, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: E abbreviates English, followed by a lime, a citrus fruit
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A French author remembers a large weight of English fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollecting' looks like remembering but signals re-collecting: L, OZ, E and LIME are rearranged as EMILEZOL, and the A that opens the clue's list is set at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Zola was the nineteenth-century French novelist of the naturalist school, an example of a French author.

clue.text: Enormous Conservative at home having sex in a reactionary manner

indicators.note: a reactionary goes backwards politically, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: home gives IN, as in staying in, and at is kept as written after it
IT is a crossword euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: A huge Tory is caught in a scandal at his house, behaving like a reactionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a reactionary manner' turns the whole string CINATIT backwards, as a reactionary looks back; 'at home' supplies IN for home plus the word at itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means of gigantic size or strength, like the Titans of Greek myth, a synonym of enormous.

clue.text: V-sign from revolutionary facing Reagan briefly

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
V, short for versus, means facing or against
Ron is the short form of Ronald, Reagan's first name

explanation.surface: A revolutionary confronting the American president makes a rude gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'V-sign' looks like the rude British two-finger gesture but means a V-shaped stripe.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe or symbol, as on a sergeant's sleeve.

clue.text: Island gathering of the clans

definitions.meaning: a French overseas department in the Indian Ocean, east of Madagascar
a get-together of family members who have been apart

explanation.surface: An island hosts a gathering of Scottish clans.
explanation.definitionFit: Réunion is an Indian Ocean island, and the ordinary word means a meeting of people long separated.

clue.text: He likes to walk, run, walk, run

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to amble is to walk slowly
R again stands for run

explanation.surface: A fitness fan alternates walking and running.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a person who goes on country walks for pleasure, a hiker.

clue.text: Nocturnal hunters regularly leaving for Wales

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: Night-time predators routinely set off for Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are birds of prey that hunt mostly at night, an example of nocturnal hunters.

clue.text: Everyone turned up to welcome a male camel's relative

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the reversed word holds the other letters
in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone arrives to greet a man who is a relation of a camel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses ALL into LLA, which takes in A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American member of the camel family, so a close relation of the camel.

clue.text: Reportedly spot female hair in sewer

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: to spot is to see
Ms is the title for a woman
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone notices a woman's hair in the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain but means one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressmaker who stitches for a living is one who sews, so a sewer in the needlework sense.

clue.text: Career of small, wee daughter

parts.note: wee and pee are both slang for urine

explanation.surface: The story of a small girl's life, from her little daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun for a working life but is the verb, to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along at full tilt, so as a noun it fits velocity.

clue.text: Bogeyman of Greeks, 50% unemployed

parts.note: O' is a short form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp

indicators.note: half the letters of Greeks are put out of work, leaving its first half

explanation.surface: Half of all Greeks are out of work, which haunts them like a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, the sort of monster used to frighten children.

clue.text: Maiden during summer month texting your boy

parts.note: in means during
AUG is August, a summer month
in text-message spelling, your is written UR
Al is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young woman texts her lover during the summer holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' looks like a girl but is the adjective, as in a maiden speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden voyage or speech is the first one, the same sense as an opening or debut event.

clue.text: Came to wonder about sanction

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wonder encloses the sanction

parts.note: awe is wonder
to OK something is to sanction or approve it

explanation.surface: Someone muses over whether to approve a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came to' reads as a total but means regained consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is to recover consciousness, which is rousing from sleep or a faint.

clue.text: Good will of good people

parts.note: a race is a people

explanation.surface: Kind intentions come from kind folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace in its sense of favour or kindliness freely given is a near synonym of goodwill.

clue.text: Supply us with a minder or nanny

indicators.note: read as supple-y, in a pliant way, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: An agency is asked to provide a childminder or a nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as provide but is the adverb from supple, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after young children, the same job as a nanny.
